Personnel Protective Equipment (safety glasses, ear protection, footwear, clothing), mild hazardous material documentation, handling and storage (coolants, alcohols etc.) training, equipment lockout tagout, guarding and most importantly training based on OSHA guidelines are required but pose no significant impediments to operation currently. Of course the above assumes current regulatory requirements and any changes in these requirements at the state of federal level could effect the degree of ES&H impact to facility operational costs and efficiency. B.1.8 Certifications and Accreditation considerations Although there are no firm certification and accreditation requirements to operating a machine shop, some counties and states may impose waste management programs upon facilities, such as the Certified Unified Program Agency (CUPA) within the purview of Los Angeles County Fire, to monitor the safe storage and disposal of certain waste products such as coolants and alcohols. Other certifications which although are not mandatory, but can benefit operations, such as: ISO9001, AS9001 or ISO13485 quality systems; or ITAR compliance may be beneficial for repurposing a machine shop to transition into other commercial work upon contract completion. At the personnel level, although no formal certification requirements exist, although staff could receive some form of certifications for job specific duties to demonstrate technical mastery or as evidence of safety training. B.2 Chemical cleaning RF cavities used in high gradient accelerators are susceptible to a phenomenon known as RF breakdown. RF breakdown is a major obstacle to higher gradient structures, limits the working power, and produces irreversible surface damage in RF components.19 As described by Pande and Singh, “During a breakdown event, the stored energy in the electromagnetic field suddenly pierces through the walls, usually in localized places, causing local melting and contamination of the surrounding surface. This results in a very fast and localized dissipation of stored energy. Durations involved in such incidence varies from tens to thousands of nanosecond.”20 The physics leading to the onset of this phenomenon are not fully understood but it is generally known that RF breakdown occurs when field emission in localized areas becomes enhanced and is sufficient to overcome the dielectric breakdown potential of the vacuum in the accelerator cavity. The sites for enhanced field emission is either an intrinsic surface feature (grain boundaries, cracks, inclusions, slip lines) or extrinstic surface feature Page 14 of 55 “Manufacturing full-scale high gradient copper accelerators: Electron beam welding and allied processes” Prepared for the U.S. Department of Energy ARDAP program (contamination, oxides, organic residues).21 Given the role of these surface defects in RF breakdown events, surface preparation is a critical factor in preventing breakdown. Achieving adequate surface preparation to reduce RF breakdown prior to the use of accelerator components is done through cleaning, baking, and conditioning. Baking and conditioning are done in-situ and after surface polishing and cleaning. Vacuum baking is performed to induce outgassing of dissolved sub-surface gases (hydrogen) that can create plasmas that lead to RF breakdown.
